summary: Submitted the corrected discriminating control for the empty-command question: the probe now actually applies the delivery-order parameter it previously ignored, collecting each recipient's messages and delivering them in the declared order (run A: 2,4,3; run B: 3,4,2) while recording the order delivered, so the same reply set is replayed with the command-carrying reply first versus last. Local native feedback already shows what the control will discriminate: both orders still leave the instance with an empty command list and no proposal, which pins the mechanism to the quorum trigger rather than to a last-reply-wins rule - the dispatch fires as soon as the recovering replica has self plus two of the three peer replies, and since only one of the three carries the owner's command, whichever two replies arrive first contain an empty one as the last-adopted value, so the empty batch is adopted in every order this message set admits. The successor experiment records that revision (previous_id = 0757162a4aa64ef4a58a90002641eb27-experiment), keeps the same scenario, prerequisites and the two per-order comparisons, and adds the decoding source range; its receipt and the corresponding interpretation update, including replacing the account's still-listed 'order variant unmeasured' limitation with the measured result, remain outstanding. Everything else in the run is unchanged: six registered questions with their accounts and receipts, four asserted defects, one holds account, the refuted wrong-row-write negative result, and nine evidence-linked behavior entries plus one Fact.
